title: Adaptive icon grid and affordance mapping for compact cost widgets
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Create a compact, adaptive iconography and affordance mapping that scales across dashboard list items, compact metric cards, and rollout rails. The goal is a single constrained grid and token mapping that supports: dense layouts, responsive density toggles, and clear interaction affordances for cost and rollout controls while meeting WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for icon and background combinations.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver Figma library file with an adaptive icon grid (6px baseline) and three density variants: dense, default, spacious
Provide a tokens page with color, size, spacing, and interaction states for each affordance (hover/focus/pressed/disabled)
Accessibility: each icon/background combo must meet 4.5:1 contrast for actionable icons in default and dense modes
Engineering handoff: exportable tokens (names + values) and a small react component spec (props + variant mapping) in Confluence
Design QA: three console screens (cost overview, rollout list, dedicated capacity card) implemented as prototypes and validated in usability pass

design_decisions: Adopt 6px baseline grid for icon spacing to align with existing compact component rhythm
Three size tokens: icon-sm (16px), icon-md (20px), icon-lg (24px). Dense mode maps to icon-sm, default to icon-md, spacious to icon-lg
Two-tone icon treatment for default and spacious modes; single-color line/icon-outline for dense to maximize legibility
Interaction affordances include: active outline token, hover elevation token, and a semitransparent focus ring token to preserve contrast
Fallback: where two-tone fails contrast in dense mode, use outline-on-solid token with increased stroke weight and adjusted token color to meet 4.5:1
